subject: Geography

source: Written for geography/y8 lesson 12 (Climate detective evidence table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 12: Earth's climate is always changing: the climate detectives. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Ice cores
points: Layers of snow build up each year
Antarctic cores go back about 800,000 years

bullets: Tree rings: wide in good years

model.title: How reliable are frost fair records as climate evidence?

parts.text: Weakness: the old London Bridge also slowed the river, so it froze more easily
Judgement: useful but must be checked with other evidence

keywords.def: a long tube of ice drilled from a glacier, holding trapped air
the last 2.6 million years of Earth's history
a cold period when ice sheets grow

questions.q: Explain how tree rings show past climate. (2 marks)
questions.a: Trees grow a ring each year (1); wide rings show good growing years, narrow rings show cold or dry years (1)

questions.q: Core: Complete the climate detective evidence table and rank the four types of evidence by reliability with reasons.
Extend: Weather diary check: write a short summary of your first week's data.
Stretch: Why does the past show that climate can change naturally, yet today's change is different?
questions.a: Natural changes were slow, over thousands of years; today's change is very fast and linked to human emissions

questions.q: Ice cores show past climate because they contain:
questions.a: B) Trapped air bubbles. Bubbles hold samples of old air, including carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Big question: how do we know the weather 100,000 years ago?
questions.a: From ice cores, pollen and other natural records that scientists date and analyse
